subject: Skylark renewal: tier realignment, uplift cap & protection bands
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@skylark.ai>
Cc: Asha Kaur <asha@skylark.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Skylark renewal: initial tier scenarios attached

Samir / Asha,

Thanks again for the productive check-in yesterday. Per our conversation I attached three renewal scenarios that reflect Skylark's current mix of short chat sessions and longer embedding workloads. High level notes:

- Scenario A (conservative): renew at current commit, smaller per-token discount slope, no uplift.
- Scenario B (recommended): modest uplift allowance, smoother per-token breakpoints to limit cliffing.
- Scenario C (growth): larger commit, steeper discount after thresholds.

You asked specifically about protection if usage falls during migration months and a cap on renewal uplift. Two quick suggestions we included in the spreadsheet: a short-term "protection band" (3 months of credit if usage is <70% of committed tokens) and an uplift ceiling (single-digit percent) to limit year-over-year step-ups.

Please review the attached Renewal_Tier_Scenarios_202611.xlsx and Skylark_Monthly_Usage_Report_202610.pdf. If you're comfortable, I'll loop in Karthik and Finance for approval on the protection mechanics and finalize the draft term sheet.

Next step: are you available for a 30-min sync Thursday to go line-by-line?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0183

Attachments: Renewal_Tier_Scenarios_202611.xlsx (spreadsheet), Skylark_Monthly_Usage_Report_202610.pdf (report)

From: Samir Patel <samir@skylark.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Skylark renewal: initial tier scenarios attached

Jordan,

Thanks for pulling these together — the scenarios are helpful. A few clarifying asks from our side:

1) Uplift cap: we want an explicit ceiling on how much the committed volume can increase at renewal without triggering a re-price conversation. Prefer something in the 5–10% range.
2) Protection band: migration to our new ingestion pipeline will likely depress usage for ~2 months. We need a guarantee that we won’t be charged full committed run-rate or lose credits on that temporary dip.
3) True-up cadence: can the true-up be quarterly rather than monthly? That reduces churn in our forecasting.

If you and Redwood can accommodate those three points we can move this to legal and aim to sign before EOY.

—Samir
Head of Platform, Skylark AI
samir@skylark.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@skylark.ai>, Asha Kaur <asha@skylark.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Skylark renewal: initial tier scenarios attached

Karthik / Lauren — looping you in. Samir asked for: 1) an uplift ceiling in the 5–10% range, 2) a short-term protection band for migration months, and 3) a preference for quarterly true-ups.

My recommendation (based on our margin modeling):
- Offer an 8% uplift ceiling at renewal (keeps price predictability for both sides).
- Protection band: 3 months of usage protection defined as credits equal to 50% of the per-token spread on the shortfall if monthly usage is below 70% of committed tokens; credits applied in the following invoice.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with a 30-day settlement window.

Pros: keeps expected ARR predictable and gives Skylark a runway for migration. Cons: small short-term revenue risk if the migration drop is prolonged.

Lauren — can Finance sign off on the credit calc above (50% of per-token spread) and the 30-day settlement? If so I’ll propose the terms to Samir and push to legal.

Jordan

Jordan / Lauren — reviewed the proposed protection mechanics. Suggest the following negotiation position to keep us within acceptable ARR risk: 

- Uplift cap: agree to 8% but add an annual true-up clause if usage exceeds +/- 20% of committed baseline (so we can reprice if their footprint materially changes).
- Protection band: convert the proposed "50% of per-token spread" credit into a capped protection credit equal to 3% of committed annualized spend for the quarter (whichever is lower). This keeps the protection predictable from a cash perspective.
- True-up cadence: quarterly is fine, but require a minimum reporting fidelity (monthly usage export) and a 45-day settlement window to ensure invoice accuracy.

If Samir accepts the 8% uplift + capped protection, I think we can get Legal to sign off quickly. I’ll own negotiation language.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
